messages:
max: starting a short thread to share results from the tenant-side watermarks + redistribution experiment. ran for 24h on slice-7; goal was to limit noisy tenants from hoarding KV residency and to measure fragmentation + long-ctx growth. dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/d/kv/watermarks (private)

sara: nice — high level numbers first? what did noisy tenants do to residency and host memory?

max: quick summary:
- noisy tenant A jumped residency from ~12% -> ~52% in 30m during a burst, host-wide KV resident pages +3.8GB
- cold tenants dropped 8-12% residency and saw token latency regress ~15th -> 75th percentile (small tail)
- fragmentation estimated ~18% (page-level) before compaction
- long-context memory growth: ~48 bytes added per token for cached entries until prefix dedupe kicks in ~4k tokens

diego: how are you measuring fragmentation? are these physical pages or logical entries?

max: physical pages. method: periodic pagewalk sampling + histogram of free fragments per page. rough CLI we used:
```
./kvstat --host slice-7 --sample 300 --pagewalk --output csv
# then postprocess to get free-run-length histogram
```
results: P_free_run_mean=3.2 slots, fragmentation_ratio=0.18

priya: config you tested for watermarks / eviction? we should be explicit so we can reproduce.

max: pushed two configs (soft/hard) and a redistribution policy that moves pages from tenants above soft_limit to a shared reclaim pool, then enforces hard_limit with aggressive compact+evict. snippet:
```
policy:
  soft_limit_pct: 0.55
  hard_limit_pct: 0.80
  redistribution: true
  eviction_strategy: lru_with_reuse_score
  reclaim_batch_pages: 128
  burst_credit_tokens: 300
```
Notes: burst_credit_tokens allow short spikes; redistribution drains 64-256 pages into shared pool per epoch.

lucy: what about fairness? did small tenants get starved because of redistribution churn? any tail latency spikes?

max: small tenants saw a small 5-10ms P95 bump during peak reclaim windows but latency returned after redistribution stabilized. We measured fairness with a new metric kv_residency_share_delta defined as max_tenant_share - median_tenant_share; it dropped from 0.42 -> 0.12 after redistribution.

diego: long-context growth: you said ~48 bytes/token. is that dominated by KV key metadata or value storage? any reuse detected when contexts repeat prefixes?

max: mostly key metadata (per-entry header + pointer alignment). reuse observed when exact prefix repeats — reuse_score >0.8 reduces new page allocations. we added a reuse_score to eviction that prefers evicting entries with low predicted reuse.

priya: did you try per-tenant soft quotas + negative-credit (borrow) with repayment window? that usually smooths bursts without global churn.

max: yes. negative-credit allowed bursts up to 15% above soft_limit, repay window 10m. reduced immediate eviction thrash but increased reclaim latency for the shared pool. combination of soft+burst+redistribution looked best.

infra-bot: experiment run complete: experiment-id=exp-2026-03-12-kwr, hosts=5, duration=24h, artifacts: s3://experiments/exp-2026-03-12-kwr/ (logs, charts). CI job 4923 passed :white_check_mark:

lucy: can we A/B this across more heterogenous workloads (embedding-heavy vs chat)? also need alerting — kv_residency_ratio > 0.7 for >5m should page infra team.

max: agreed. next steps I propose:
- roll A/B to 20 hosts (mix of E4/E8 instances) for 48h
- add metric kv_residency_ratio, kv_residency_share_delta to console and alert on >0.7 and >0.25 respectively
- tune reclaim_batch_pages per instance type (smaller on E4)
- add compaction schedule to target fragmentation >0.15

sara: thanks, this is actionable. please post small repro recipe and exact config in the experiment S3 and mention owners. :thumbsup:

max: done — uploaded configs and owners file. ping me if you want copies or raw CSVs.
